name: Kalsubai Peak
description: Maharashtra's highest peak at 1,646m, near Bhandardara. A steady climb through five iron ladders with sweeping Sahyadri views from the summit temple.
how_to_reach: Drive to Bari village via Igatpuri or Bhandardara road; trailhead starts from Bari.

name: Rajmachi Trek
description: Twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) reached via a forested trail from Lonavala, popular for monsoon greenery and a night trek option.
how_to_reach: From Lonavala, drive/hike to Udhewadi base village via Tungarli or Kondhane route.

name: Harishchandragad
description: A demanding climb to an ancient hill fort, famous for the Konkan Kada cliff and the Kedareshwar cave temple.
how_to_reach: Base villages Khireshwar or Pachnai, reached via Kalyan-Ahmednagar road.

name: Sinhagad Fort
description: An easy, popular trek right outside Pune with a motorable road option too, known for kanda bhaji and hilltop views.
how_to_reach: Drive from Pune via Khadakwasla to the base, then a short climb or road to the top.

name: Lohagad Fort
description: A beginner-friendly fort trek near Lonavala with a stepped path, monsoon waterfalls en route, and the famous Vinchu Kata spur.
how_to_reach: From Malavli station or Lonavala, drive to Lohagadwadi base village.

name: Kondhari Waterfall
description: A tucked-away waterfall near Bhor, gushing hard through the monsoon with a short walk from the nearest road.
how_to_reach: Drive to Bhor via NH4, then follow local roads toward the falls.

name: Tamhini Waterfall
description: Roadside and trail waterfalls through the Tamhini Ghat, one of the greenest monsoon drives near Pune.
how_to_reach: Drive from Pune via Mulshi towards Tamhini Ghat road.

name: Devkund Waterfall
description: A two-tiered waterfall near Bhira reached by a river-crossing trail through the forest, one of the tallest in the region.
how_to_reach: Drive to Bhira village, then trek roughly 5km along the stream to the falls.

name: Randha Falls
description: A dramatic horseshoe-shaped waterfall near Bhandardara, easily viewable from a roadside deck.
how_to_reach: On the main Bhandardara road, a short walk from the parking area.

name: Pawna Lake Camping
description: The classic Mumbai-Pune weekend campsite: lakeside tents facing Tikona and Lohagad forts, with bonfires and DJ nights on weekends.
how_to_reach: Drive via Lonavala or Kamshet to the Pawna Dam backwater campsites.

name: Bhandardara Camping
description: Quiet lakeside camping by Arthur Lake at the base of Kalsubai, with pine groves and cleaner night skies than most weekend spots.
how_to_reach: Drive via Igatpuri or Sangamner to Bhandardara village and the lakeside camps.

name: Kamshet Camping
description: Hillside campsites known for sunrise paragliding, overlooking the Indrayani valley near Lonavala.
how_to_reach: Drive to Kamshet on the old Mumbai-Pune highway, campsites are a short climb off the road.

name: Rajmachi Camping
description: Tent stays at Udhewadi village beneath Rajmachi fort, popular for a combined monsoon trek-and-camp weekend.
how_to_reach: Drive/hike from Lonavala to Udhewadi village, campsites are run by local homestays.
